notes: §1985:IX.4.3.3 SR2: "The INVALID KEY phrase must be specified for a DELETE statement which references a file which is not in sequential access mode and for which an applicable USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure is not specified." BindDelete calls ExceptionPhraseRequirement.Require (InForce below 2002), which refuses with COBOL6826 unless the INVALID KEY phrase is written, the file is in sequential access mode, or HasApplicableUse finds a USE naming the file or a mode it can be open in; an EXTEND procedure counts only when FileModel.CanOpenExtend holds, which closes PB5413's EXTEND arm that left this row PARTIAL. 'Applicable' is read as the earlier adjudication settled it (a procedure that names the file or a mode the file can be open in; held-85/set6). Probes at 85 (work-rs-04/c6, c4): b) random and dynamic DELETE with no phrase and no USE, with only NOT INVALID KEY, with only a USE ON EXTEND, and with only a USE naming another file are COBOL6826; e) sequential access DELETE with no phrase compiles and runs (status 00); random/dynamic with INVALID KEY runs IK; with USE ON IFILE or ON I-O the absent key runs USE 23 then continues; with USE ON INPUT or ON OUTPUT it compiles and the 23 passes to the next statement (no procedure applies at run time, GR3's undefined case); a/c/d/f do not reach a statement with only a file-name operand. The witness is the refusal of a random DELETE with no INVALID KEY and no USE. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming kb/Work PB5021 (landed), kb/Work PB5413 (landed); the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5413 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-04.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-04-refute.json).

next.reason: §1985:IX.4.3.3 SR2: 'The INVALID KEY phrase must be specified for a DELETE statement which references a file which is not in sequential access mode and for which an applicable USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure is not specified' (indexed file). 2023 has no such syntax rule (§2023:14.9.10.3 SR2 only forbids the phrase in sequential access mode); §2023:14.9.10.4 GR11 makes the transfer of control depend 'on the presence or absence of the optional INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY phrases in the DELETE RECORD statement as specified in 9.1.14', and the refused case is stated by §2023:9.1.14 GR4: 'If the INVALID KEY phrase is not specified in the input-output statement and there are no applicable exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement'; so too §2023:9.1.14 GR3: 'If control is returned from those statements or there are no applicable exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement'. Words that differ: 1985 'must be specified'; 2023 'not specified ... there are no applicable ... exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end'. A statement 1985 refuses is accepted by 2023 with a stated run-time effect: a lifted refusal, so CHANGED (kb/Work PB5021), not REMOVED.
